title: Report Generation Module Architecture
description: This page details the architecture and functionality of the Report Generation Module. The module fetches transactional data, applies business filters, and generates reports in both PDF and Excel. The backend is built using Spring Boot with microservice principles, exposing endpoints for generating, previewing, and downloading reports. Frontend will provide dynamic filtering and grouping features. Error tracking is integrated with Splunk and ELK. Reports are cached for 24 hours using Redis for performance optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Reports must be generated in under 10 seconds for 10,000 records.
Support download in both PDF and Excel formats with company branding.
Include dynamic filters like date range, client ID, transaction type.
Must include pagination and total counts in reports.
Only authorized users can trigger report generation.
Audit log entries must be generated for every report request.
Errors must return clear messages and codes (e.g., 400, 403, 500).

title: Data Ingestion Pipeline (Client Reference Data)
description: This page documents the design of the data ingestion service for client reference data. Data is fetched from an upstream vendor API and passed through a validation and transformation layer. Valid records are upserted into MongoDB. A backup of the raw feed is saved to an S3 bucket. Ingestion failures trigger alerts via PagerDuty. Kafka topics are used to notify downstream systems. The pipeline is built using Spring Batch with retry logic, schema validation, and duplicate detection.
acceptance_criteria: Service should poll vendor API every 15 minutes.
Validation errors must be logged and skipped, not block the batch.
Each batch must be stored as a backup in S3 with timestamp.
Kafka message must be published for each valid record ingested.
Deduplication must prevent inserting existing records.
Dashboard should display ingestion rate and error count.
SLA: 95% of records processed in <1 min; alert if breached.

title: Authentication and Authorization Microservice
description: The purpose of this Confluence page is to design the authentication and role-based authorization microservice. It supports JWT-based login with refresh tokens and LDAP fallback. Roles are managed via an internal admin dashboard. Service integrates with Keycloak for OAuth2.0 compliance. All token activity is audited. The microservice is containerized using Docker and deployed in a separate namespace to reduce blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Supports login using email/password and LDAP SSO fallback.
JWT tokens expire in 15 minutes; refresh token expires in 7 days.
Supports RBAC with roles like Admin, User, ReadOnly.
Logout should blacklist active JWT token.
Rate limit login attempts to 5 per minute per user.
Provide Swagger UI for login, refresh, and validate endpoints.
Audit trail for login/logout actions must be stored for 90 days.

title: User Preferences Service
description: This page outlines the user preferences microservice that stores configuration such as theme, language, and notification preferences. The service provides CRUD operations and integrates with MongoDB. Preferences are loaded during login and cached using Redis. Preference changes trigger event publication to allow real-time updates in the UI. API layer is secured using OAuth 2.0 access tokens.
acceptance_criteria: GET /preferences should return user-specific settings in under 200ms.
PUT /preferences should persist settings and return success message.
Redis cache must invalidate on preference update.
Preferences schema must support key/value flexibility.
API must be protected using bearer token.
Notification service must receive preference change event.
Include unit and integration tests for all endpoints.

title: Trade Reconciliation Service
description: The reconciliation service compares internal trades against broker feed to identify mismatches. Differences are highlighted via a UI, and reconciliation history is maintained. The service provides APIs to fetch match status, update trade states, and export results. It runs in batch mode every night. Historical reconciliation data is archived in a cold storage system after 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: Must reconcile at least 1 million trades in 30 minutes.
Support filtering by trade date, security ID, and broker.
Mismatch reason must be clearly indicated in output.
Allow manual override and reprocessing of trades.
UI must show reconciliation result with timestamps.
All mismatched trades must be marked for retry.
Cold storage archiving job must run weekly.

title: Notification Service (Email/SMS/Slack)
description: This Confluence page captures the design and functionality of a centralized notification system. It supports sending emails, SMS, and Slack messages based on triggers from upstream services. Templates are customizable. Throttling and retries are built-in. Logs are persisted to ElasticSearch. Notification preferences are respected at all times, with fallback channels configured.
acceptance_criteria: Emails must be delivered via SendGrid within 5 seconds.
SMS fallback must trigger after email failure.
Slack messages must contain hyperlink and custom buttons.
Logs should store recipient, channel, and status.
Rate limit to 100 notifications/min/channel.
Allow resend with same payload within 2 minutes cooldown.
Templates must support parameterized placeholders.

title: Audit Logging Framework
description: The audit logging framework ensures traceability for user and system actions. It supports structured logs, JSON format, and integration with ELK stack. Logs are stored with user ID, timestamp, IP, and request context. A masking layer is applied to hide sensitive fields. Logs are queryable via Kibana dashboards for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: All user actions must be logged with request ID and timestamp.
Sensitive fields like password must be masked.
Logs should be shipped to ElasticSearch within 10 seconds.
Retry logic must support 3 attempts for failed log writes.
Kibana dashboards must support filtering by user ID and action type.
Logs must be retained for 1 year for compliance.

title: Client Onboarding Workflow
description: This document defines the multi-step workflow for client onboarding, including KYC document upload, digital signature, and internal approvals. The workflow is powered by a Camunda BPM engine. Email notifications are sent for pending actions. Status is tracked via a dashboard. The frontend offers a form-based wizard interface for smooth onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow must include 5 steps: KYC, docs, e-sign, review, approval.
Each step must be time-bound (max 48h) or auto-escalate.
Incomplete onboarding attempts must auto-expire after 7 days.
KYC documents must be scanned for fraud and stored encrypted.
UI must reflect current step and estimated time remaining.
Audit trail must include who approved which step with timestamp.
Mobile responsive UI must be available.

title: Data Retention Policy Implementation
description: The purpose of this document is to define how data retention rules are applied across all services. Each data category has its own TTL policy, ranging from 7 days to 7 years. The deletion is automated via scheduled jobs that archive or purge old data. Legal hold and audit exclusion lists are respected. Configuration is maintained via YAML files version-controlled in Git.
acceptance_criteria: Purge job must run daily at midnight without manual trigger.
All deletions must be logged and recoverable for 7 days.
Support legal hold exclusions based on client or record ID.
YAML-based config must be validated before deployment.
Notifications must be sent before large deletions (>1GB).
Dashboard must show deleted vs. archived count per service.
Policy changes must require 2-step approval.

title: API Gateway Setup and Routing Rules
description: This page outlines the setup of an API Gateway using Kong to handle traffic routing, security, and logging across all services. Features include rate limiting, IP whitelisting, JWT auth, and CORS configuration. APIs are documented using OpenAPI and exposed via Swagger UI. Gateway metrics are collected via Prometheus for performance monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: All services must be reachable via /api/{service-name} routes.
Rate limit must be configurable per consumer (default 100/min).
JWT validation must reject expired or malformed tokens.
Log headers must include request ID and user-agent.
Add CORS headers to allow all GET requests from frontend.
Latency for gateway requests should be under 100ms.
Service health checks must be configurable via UI.

title: Exception Handling Strategy for Microservices
description: This Confluence page outlines a consistent exception handling strategy across all backend microservices. Each service implements a global error handler that classifies exceptions into client errors (4xx), server errors (5xx), and custom business exceptions. A standard error response schema includes error code, message, and correlation ID. Alerts are triggered on critical failures and logged in ELK. Developers are advised to use functional-style try-catch blocks to manage downstream dependencies, including database and third-party APIs.
acceptance_criteria: All 4xx and 5xx errors must return a standard JSON error format.
Each error must include a unique correlation ID in the response.
Unhandled exceptions must be caught by the global handler.
Stack traces should not be exposed to the client.
Critical 5xx errors must trigger Slack alerts via webhook.
All errors must be logged to ELK with trace-level metadata.
Retry logic must apply only to idempotent operations.

title: File Upload and Virus Scanning Module
description: This module enables users to upload documents, images, and PDFs as part of workflows such as onboarding and KYC. Files are scanned for viruses using ClamAV before being accepted. Uploaded files are stored securely in AWS S3 with encrypted paths and signed URLs. Maximum upload size is 20MB per file. Progress bars and drag-drop support are provided in the UI. Invalid files are rejected with user-friendly messages and are not persisted.
acceptance_criteria: Allow upload of .pdf, .docx, .png, and .jpg only.
Reject files larger than 20MB with appropriate error message.
All uploads must pass ClamAV virus scan before storage.
File storage must use encrypted S3 buckets with versioning.
Signed URLs must expire within 10 minutes of generation.
UI must show file preview and allow re-upload option.
Audit log must capture filename, size, uploader, and result.

title: Real-Time Dashboard with WebSockets
description: This document explains the implementation of a real-time metrics dashboard for operational teams. The dashboard receives live updates via WebSocket pushed from backend services using a publish-subscribe mechanism. The backend maintains client sessions, periodically sends health checks, and disconnects inactive clients after timeout. The UI is built in React with dynamic charts rendered using Chart.js. All incoming data is sanitized before rendering to prevent XSS attacks.
acceptance_criteria: WebSocket must support bi-directional messaging over secure (wss) protocol.
Dashboard must auto-refresh without page reload.
Inactivity timeout should disconnect clients after 15 minutes.
Display latency < 1s between event trigger and UI update.
Charts must auto-scale and support zoom/filter controls.
All WebSocket payloads must be schema validated.
Provide fallback to REST polling if WebSocket fails.

title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture Guidelines
description: This page lays out design principles for building a multi-tenant SaaS platform. Tenants are logically isolated at the database level with row-level access control and shared schema. All configurations such as themes, limits, and API keys are scoped to the tenant context. The authentication layer includes tenant-aware token issuance. Audit logs and metrics are also tagged per tenant. Tenant provisioning is automated through Terraform scripts. Resource limits are applied using Kubernetes quotas.
acceptance_criteria: Each request must carry a valid tenant ID in the header.
All database queries must filter by tenant ID.
Audit logs and metrics must include tenant-specific tags.
Kubernetes resource quotas must restrict per-tenant CPU and memory.
Provisioning pipeline must support creating tenant infra in <2 mins.
Support per-tenant custom branding in UI via config service.
Error messages must never leak tenant identifiers.

title: PDF Generation Engine using Headless Chrome
description: This Confluence page describes the service responsible for generating high-quality PDFs from HTML templates using Puppeteer (headless Chrome). The service queues PDF jobs, supports batch export, and allows embedding charts and dynamic elements. All templates are customizable and pulled from a config repo. Rendered PDFs are uploaded to S3 and linked in user portals. The engine auto-scales using horizontal pod autoscaler based on job queue size.
acceptance_criteria: Support margin, header, and footer config per template.
PDFs must retain pixel-perfect layout as per HTML source.
Batch mode must support generating 100 PDFs in <2 mins.
Errors must provide clear feedback with line number and template ID.
Store generated files in S3 with access logs.
Expose retry API for failed jobs with idempotency key.
Queue metrics must be visible in Prometheus dashboard.
